title: Centre proposes freeze on Lok Sabha seat proportions for States until 2051
author: Varghese K. George ,Nistula Hebbar
content_html:
A new Constitutional Amendment Bill approved by the Union Cabinet on Friday (November 27, 2026) proposes an extension of the existing freeze on the inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats for another 25 years, until 2051, addressing the core concern of States that feared a loss of their proportionate strength due to the decline in their share of the national population.

Also read | Lok Sabha seat freeze is no longer linked to population stabilisation

The 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill marks a significant turn from the 131st Amendment Bill moved by the Centre in April 2026 that sought to redistribute Lok Sabha seats among States according to the 2011 Census population.

The proposed amendment removes the linkage of the existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats to the 1971 Census and links it with provisions related to women’s reservation in Article 334A of the Constitution. The guarantee for a 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats for each State is being written into this, providing that, for the purposes of giving immediate effect to such reservation for women, “the delimitation so undertaken shall provide for an increase of fifty per cent in the number of seats allocated to each State and Union territory in the House of the People.” The total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State and Union territory will also increase similarly, “over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation”.

The new Bill, accompanied by a fresh Delimitation Bill, proposes to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats in each State by 50%, while the maximum strength of the lower House will rise from the current 550 to 850. If these Bills are passed by Parliament in its special sittings from November 30 to December 3, the path to immediate delimitation will open, which will also bring into force the 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha.

Amendments to Articles 81 and 82, which mandate the size and distribution of Lok Sabha seats among the States, propose to extend a sunset clause for the existing proportion until 2051.

The existing provision in Article 82 that says that “until the relevant figures for the first census taken after the year 2026 have been published, it shall not be necessary to readjust” the distribution of seats is being amended in the Bill and will be changed to read “until the year 2051”.

Article 82 currently has two definitions for population: for the purposes of distribution among States, the 1971 population; and for the purposes of delimitation of individual constituencies within the States, the 2001 Census. The proposed amendment will extend the sunset clause to “until the year 2051”, but the reference to the 1971 Census has been dropped.

The Bill proposes that the distribution among States will be determined “in accordance with Article 334A”, while the boundaries of individual constituencies will be determined by the “latest published census figures available on the date of the commencement of the Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 2026”.

title: Centre’s delimitation fix steadies Yogi Adityanath’s nerves ahead of polls
author: Anuj Kumar
content_html:
Following the Union Cabinet’s approval of a revised Delimitation Bill ahead of the upcoming special sitting of Parliament, Uttar Pradesh’s state legislature is set to expand beyond the long-standing constitutional ceiling of 500 members without the state being divided.

In the corridors of power in Lucknow and New Delhi, the move is seen as a signal by the BJP’s central leadership to put persistent speculation over the division of Uttar Pradesh to rest and steady nerves inside Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s camp ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.

title: What is the Indraprastha Communique issued after SCO Civilizational Forum in New Delhi? | Explained
author: Sreeparna Chakrabarty
content_html:
The Story So Far: India hosted the first “Civilisational Dialogue Forum” of the 10-nation Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) grouping, that includes Pakistan, from November 20-22 at Delhi’s historic Purana Qila. The dialogue, which was organized by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of External Affairs, was proposed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the SCO leaders’ Summit in Tianjin last year and adopted by the SCO Council. At the end of the three-day summit, member countries adopted an outcome document — ‘Indraprastha Communiqué’ — which recognised culture as a vital bridge of friendship and good-neighbourliness among the nations and an important dimension of cooperation.

The SCO civilizational dialogue was proposed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and endorsed by SCO Council of Heads of Government. It aims to strengthen people to people ties and promote dialogue on the shared civilisational, cultural and intellectual heritage of the SCO region.

title: Ten pillars of Nepal-India vision statement issued during Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit
author: Kallol Bhattacherjee
content_html:
Story so far: Former singer and media personality, Balendra Shah became the Prime Minister of Nepal in March this year after an election that saw the Rastriya Swatantra Party win a two-thirds majority in the Nepali parliament. The election was held after an interim administration which took charge after the Gen-Z uprising of September 2025 toppled the K. P. Sharma Oli-led Communist Party of Nepal - Unified Marxist–Leninist (CPN-UML) -Nepali Congress government. The defeat of the Maoist parties and the Nepali Congress marked a significant shift in Nepal’s nearly two decades long democratic journey following the abolition of the monarchy.

Before the uprising Nepali politics was dominated by Maoist parties and leaders like Pushpakamal Dahal ‘Prachanda’, K P Sharma Oli, Madhav Nepal, Baburam Bhattarai alongside the leaders of the Nepali Congress. But the defeat of the so called mainstream political parties by a relatively new political party has created a less ideologically charged moment in Nepali politics as RSP is not known for any ideological rigour and orthodoxy.

The Vision Document appears to take advantage of Nepal’s uprising against the Maoist parties and the Nepali Congress and highlights a “forward looking” approach, meaning the measures agreed with Maoist and NC Prime Ministers will not be part of the agenda that is being shaped under Prime Minister Shah.

Mr. Shah’s focus has been on making a new start domestically and he had said earlier that he would focus on domestic issues but later changed his stance and visited the US in September to participate in the UNGA session where he talked about climate justice following the devastating floods in Bhotekoshi river.

In November first week, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri visited Kathmandu and reiterated India’s invite to PM Shah following which Prime Minister Shah came on a two-day trip to New Delhi. During the visit a ten pillared vision statement was issued giving new direction to the relationship for the post-uprising Nepal.

title: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Laxmi Verma injured in car accident in Chhattisgarh
author: Shubhomoy Sikdar
content_html:
Laxmi Verma, a BJP Rajya Sabha member from Chhattisgarh, was injured after her car collided with another vehicle in Chhattisgarh's Raipur district, police said on Saturday (November 28, 2026).

The accident happened late on Friday (November 27, 2026) evening on the Balodabazar-Raipur Road in Kharora area while Ms Verma was returning after attending a programme in her native Balodabazar-Bhatapara district, said a police officer.

The MP's son and a security staff member were also travelling in the car at the time.

The injured were taken to a hospital, and Verma was shifted to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Raipur, according to the police.

An AIIMS public relations officer told journalists that Ms Verma had suffered a fracture. The MP wrote about the accident on her official account on X describing the incident as a close shave and stating that the injury sustained by her was minor.

“By God's grace, a major accident was averted yesterday. Of the four of us travelling in the vehicle, the driver, personal assistant, and personal security guard are completely safe and sound. I only suffered a minor injury to my right hand. After treatment at AIIMS Raipur, I will return to my residence soon. I am grateful to well-wishers, senior leaders, fellow workers, and media colleagues for their well-wishes. It is because of your good wishes that I am safe today,” she wrote in Hindi.

    Delimitation long-term plan for forever fascism: Arundhati Roy

    Booker Prize-winning author Arundhati Roy criticised the government’s motives behind the delimitation bill and claimed it is a long-term plan for “forever fascism” that will break the back of democracy.

    Ms. Roy was speaking at the National Conclave of Writers, Artists and Cultural Practitioners at Jawahar Bhawan.

    “Delimitation will break the back of democracy. Do not let them fool you into believing that it is just about increasing the number of constituencies and the number of MPs. Do not believe that the women’s bill has anything to do with women’s rights. This has to do with redrawing the map of constituencies to consolidate the divisions of caste, religion and community,” she claimed.

    Ms. Roy said what has been happening in the country is “democratic fascism, in which fascists are trying to murder the meaning of democracy”.

    - PTI

    Mayawati welcomes Centre’s move for 33% women’s quota in Parliament

    BSP chief Mayawati welcomed the Centre’s move to facilitate 33% reservation for women in Parliament and State Assemblies, but demanded a separate quota for women from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

    In a long post on X in Hindi, the former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister said it would have been a historic step if women from SC and ST communities, who have faced exploitation and neglect for centuries, had been given separate reservation within the proposed quota.

    “It would have been good, rather historic, if separate reservation had been provided within this quota for women from SC and ST communities, who have been exploited, oppressed and neglected for centuries,” she said.

    She urged the Centre to consider the demand sympathetically, saying it would be an appropriate and just step.

    Ms. Mayawati said the BSP had consistently championed women’s dignity, security and adequate representation in politics, in keeping with the egalitarian ideals of the Constitution framed under the leadership of B. R. Ambedkar.

    Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan expressed support for the proposed delimitation reform, saying it would strengthen democratic representation by giving every state and region an adequate voice in Parliament.

    The Deputy CM said a stronger democracy is built when every citizen is heard, and every state moves forward with confidence.

    “The proposed delimitation reform will strengthen democratic representation by ensuring that every state and region has an adequate voice in Parliament,” said Kalyan in a post on X late on Friday (November 27, 2026).

    According to the Deputy CM, the proposal reflected the spirit of cooperative federalism by recognising the contributions and progress of different states while ensuring that their parliamentary representation was protected.

    Congress' Madhu Goud vows to oppose 50% seat hike

    The proposed 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats has triggered a political divide, with Congress leader Madhu Yashki Goud alleging that the move would put southern states at a permanent disadvantage

    Opposing the proposed increase, Mr. Goud said the Congress, along with its INDIA bloc partners, would fight the Bill during the upcoming Special Session of Parliament, arguing that the Centre had not consulted southern states or Opposition parties before taking the decision.

    Calling the proposal unconstitutional, the Congress leader accused the Centre of not taking Opposition parties into confidence and said the decision raised concerns over cooperative federalism.

    “This is absolutely unconstitutional. The Centre is behaving like a dictator. It has never discussed the matter or taken Opposition parties into confidence. This is in the interest of the nation and will bring in cooperative federalism. Give equal opportunities to the southern states, rather than putting them in a disadvantaged position. The Centre should have consulted the southern states and Opposition parties,” he said.

    Special Parliament sitting eyes Assembly elections: Tejashwi

    RJD working president Tejashwi Yadav has voiced suspicion that the upcoming special sitting of Parliament may have been called with an eye on Assembly elections, due in a few months, in several states.

    Talking to reporters here on Friday (November 27, 2026), Mr. Yadav, also the Leader of Opposition in the Bihar Assembly, made it clear that his party would stick to its “old stand” on the delimitation bill, which, according to reports, may be tabled in Parliament afresh.

    “It may be that the sitting has been called in view of the elections,” said the former Deputy Chief Minister, upon being asked whether he thought the ruling BJP-led NDA might try to cash in on the issue of women’s reservation, linked to the Bill, in the assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh and Punjab.

    Asked about his party’s stand on the bill, which needs a two-thirds majority to get cleared, the RJD leader said, “It would have been better had the government taken all political groups into confidence. Nonetheless, our old stand is known to all.”

    Mr. Yadav, also a key INDIA bloc partner, sought to make light of Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s call for implementation of the Uniform Civil Code in all BJP-ruled states.

title: Woman files three nominations for pradhan’s post in Rajasthan’s Deeg; elected unopposed on BJP ticket
author: PTI
content_html:
A woman candidate filed three nominations for the post of pradhan of Brij Nagar Panchayat Samiti in Rajasthan's Deeg district as a Congress, BJP and Independent candidate before eventually being elected unopposed on a BJP ticket.

The unusual political development prompted former Congress MLA Wajib Ali to resign from his post as a Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) member, taking moral responsibility for the party's failure to secure the pradhan's post.

Bati Kumari initially filed her nomination as a Congress candidate in the presence of Mr. Ali. She later arrived with BJP leader Jawahar Singh Bedham and filed another nomination as the BJP candidate. She also submitted a third nomination as an Independent.

As no other candidate entered the contest, Bati Kumari subsequently withdrew her Congress and Independent nominations and was declared elected unopposed as the BJP candidate.

Following the development, Mr. Ali accused the BJP of using money power and misusing its position in government to secure the victory.

He alleged that the BJP had deceived Congress by taking away its candidate after she had already filed her nomination.

"The Congress candidate came with us wearing a saree. But the BJP got her clothes changed and brought her back as its candidate to win the election," Mr. Ali alleged.

He said the BJP did not win through a democratic process but through deception.

"The Congress had the people's mandate to elect its pradhan, but the BJP scripted an entire drama to take away our candidate," he alleged.

Mr. Ali said he was taking moral responsibility for the party's failure and had resigned from his PCC membership.

He also apologised to Congress workers who were disappointed by the outcome.

The former MLA said he would continue working for the Congress as an ordinary party worker without holding any organisational position.

Rejecting the allegations, BJP district president Satish Bansal said Bati Kumari had filed her nomination as the party's candidate and was elected unopposed.

"It is a splendid victory for the BJP in Brij Nagar. Bati Kumari filed her nomination as our candidate and won unopposed," Mr. Bansal said.

He termed Mr. Ali's allegations baseless and advised him to use restrained language.

title: Telangana to unveil 11 new policies at Global Summit
author: R. Ravikanth Reddy
content_html:
The Telangana government is preparing to unveil 11 new policies covering industry, information technology and higher education at the upcoming Invest Telangana Global Summit, as part of its efforts to accelerate industrial growth and attract investments into emerging sectors.

The policies have been formulated in line with the Telangana Rising Vision 2047, which aims to transform the State into a $3 trillion economy by 2047. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy had unveiled the vision document at last year’s Global Summit, outlining the State’s long-term economic and development goals.

The proposed Industrial Policy 2.0 will seek to expand the manufacturing base and strengthen Telangana’s position as an investment destination. Special policies are being prepared for labour-intensive sectors such as textiles and apparel, footwear and leather products, with the objective of generating large-scale employment.

The government is also focusing on attracting fresh investments into aerospace, defence and space industries, in which Telangana has already established a presence. A dedicated logistics policy is being developed to strengthen industrial transportation, warehousing and supply-chain infrastructure.

The IT sector will receive particular attention, given Hyderabad’s growing prominence as a global technology hub. The IT department is preparing a comprehensive ICT Policy 2.0, along with dedicated policies for Global Capability Centres (GCCs), data centres, electronics and semiconductors.

A separate Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics (AVGC) policy is also being planned to encourage investments and promote emerging creative technology industries.

In the education sector, the government intends to facilitate reputed foreign higher education institutions in establishing offshore campuses. The proposed policy aims to bring international-standard education and research opportunities closer to students in Telangana, reducing the need to travel abroad for quality higher education.

The 11 policies to be unveiled at the summit include Industrial Policy 2.0; Footwear and Leather Policy; Textiles and Apparel Policy 2.0; Aerospace, Defence and Space Policy; Logistics Policy; ICT Policy 2.0; GCC Policy; Data Centres Policy 2.0; Electronics and Semiconductors Policy; AVGC Policy; and Foreign Higher Education Institutions Offshore Campus Policy.

title: Gutkha worth ₹66.78 lakh seized from container in Thane’s Kalwa; driver arrested, seven others wanted
author: Yohaan Varghese
content_html:
The Kalwa police on Thursday (November 26, 2026) arrested a 32-year-old container driver for allegedly transporting banned gutkha worth ₹66.78 lakh after intercepting a vehicle near Parsik Circle in Kalwa. The police seized the gutkha along with the container, collectively valued at ₹94.78 lakh, and launched a search for seven other accused allegedly involved in the illegal transportation and distribution of the banned product.

According to the police, the operation was carried out at around 1:40 p.m. on November 26 after a team intercepted a suspicious Eicher container bearing registration number TG-12-U-1611 opposite Amit Garden on the Mumbra-Bhiwandi carriageway.

During the inspection, police found that fans, hardware materials, and other goods had allegedly been used to conceal the consignment and evade detection. A thorough search of the vehicle led to the recovery of 19,080 packets of banned ‘Gold 9000’ gutkha packed in 53 large sacks.

The seized gutkha was valued at ₹66.78 lakh, while the container was worth ₹28 lakh.

The arrested accused has been identified as Mehraj Karim Shaikh, 32, a resident of Bhiwandi and a native of Hyderabad.

Based on a complaint lodged by Food Safety Officer Aruna Veerkayade, the Kalwa police registered an FIR under relevant provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.

Police are searching for seven other accused, including those allegedly involved in the manufacture, transportation and distribution of the banned gutkha. Investigators are also looking into the source of the consignment and its intended destination.

The seizure could potentially help uncover a larger gutkha smuggling and distribution network, with investigators probing the alleged involvement of manufacturers, transporters and distributors.

Assistant Police Inspector Santosh Pimple of the Kalwa police station is conducting further investigations.
